title: Korean Cod Jeon Sliders
changes_from_base: Thin slices of cod are dusted in flour, dipped in beaten egg and gently pan-fried as Korean jeon, then tucked into soft sweet rolls with sesame mayonnaise, a soy-dressed spring onion salad and dill pickles in place of a beef patty and cheese.
summary: Delicate white fish fillet, thinly sliced and pan-fried until golden, served with crisp salad and a subtle sesame accent.

ingredients.item: thick cod fillet, cut on the diagonal into 8 slices about 1 cm thick
fine sea salt or table salt
spring onions, halved lengthways and thinly sliced on the diagonal

steps.title: Dressing
steps.text: Whisk together 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp white vinegar and ¼ tsp toasted sesame oil in a small bowl.

steps.title: Mayo
steps.text: Stir 1¼ tsp toasted sesame oil into 120 g mayonnaise in another small bowl.

steps.title: Dredge
steps.text: Put 3 tbsp plain flour in one shallow bowl and beat 1 large egg in another; season 225 g thick cod fillet cut diagonally into 8 slices about 1 cm thick with ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp ground black pepper, dredge in flour, shake off excess, then set each slice on a large plate.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 30 ml neutral oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium; dip each floured cod slice in beaten egg and lay in the hot oil, cook for 2-3 min per side until golden, opaque throughout and 63 °C in the centre, then drain on kitchen paper and salt lightly.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Toss 2 halved and thinly sliced spring onions and 20 g tender baby salad leaves in the soy dressing.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spread sesame mayonnaise on 8 split soft sweet dinner roll bottoms, add the dressed salad, a piece of fried cod, sliced dill pickles and the roll tops.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Eat straight away whilst the jeon is warm, or within 2 hours at room temperature if preferred.

tips: Slice the cod diagonally and at an even thickness for consistent cooking throughout
Dip each slice in egg immediately before frying so the coating adheres properly
Serve the sliders warm for the best contrast between the hot, crispy fish and cool, fresh toppings
storage: The fried fish is best served warm, but can be eaten at room temperature within 2 hours of cooking.
